diagnostics.question: DKT wins the aggregate metrics and loses the learning curve. Which of six hypotheses explains it, and what does each measure say?
diagnostics.protocol: identical held-out rows to metrics.json (every test interaction except each student's first); DKT reproduced from the committed weights with a numpy forward pass, BKT refitted by EM on the training split
diagnostics.baselines_note: global_rate, skill_rate, student_rate and skill_and_student contain no notion of practice on a skill. They are the control: a model whose curve looks like theirs has not learned learning.

raw_curve.note: every held-out row, bucketed by opportunity. Later buckets average a different, more persistent population than earlier ones — see the cohort curve.

cohort_curve.note: only (student, skill) pairs with at least 10 attempts, restricted to their first 10. Same population at every point.

position_slices.note: held-out rows sliced by absolute position in the student's sequence

evidence_response.note: change in the predicted probability for a skill, from just before to just after an answer on that skill. A model that updates on evidence separates correct from wrong; near-zero means the answer changed nothing.

consistency.note: Yeung & Yeung (2018): w1/w2 measure how much the whole prediction vector thrashes between answers; reconstruction_error is the gap between the prediction for the skill just answered and that answer.
